title: Who's Right?
tagline: Every expert disagrees. The crowd already knows.
asset_type: cinematic video ad (vertical 9:16, mutable scans to 16:9)
concept_overview: A 42-second cinematic spot that opens on a brutal montage of talking-head pundits each shouting a different market call (Buy! Sell! Crash! To the moon!). The emotional undertone is the silent crisis of the modern solo retail trader: more information than ever, but no closer to a decision, glued to screens at 1am while conflicting signals pull them apart. The turn exposes the truth that moves markets is not any one oracle but the crowd itself, and CrowdWisdom is the only tool that converts that crowd into one clear, auditable decision: entry, stop, target. Ends on a clean brand card and a low-friction free-trial CTA. Creative premise is distinct from our prior 'You're Not Guessing Alone' spot (solo-trader + signal fatigue): this one leads with expert-conflict and the measurable contagion of decision paralysis, anchored to a live sentiment extreme.
ad_channel: Meta feed / Reels / TikTok / YouTube Shorts — sound-on-first-2s, subtitles burned in at all times

ideal_customer_profile.who: Jess, 34, self-directed retail trader (equities + options), 3-6 years in the market, trades nights/weekends around a day job.
ideal_customer_profile.frustration: Subscribed to 3 research tools (a charting platform, an analyst-rating feed, an options-education newsletter) and a paid Telegram signal group. Still starts Monday without a clear position. Sleepless nights reconciling contradicting outlooks; has overtraded out of boredom and chased pumps out of FOMO.
ideal_customer_profile.what_they_already_believe: That real money is made by 'knowing something others don't', so they keep hoarding more data. They have not yet realized the edge is collective consensus, not more data.
ideal_customer_profile.why_now: September volatility + a record bearish-reading spike (see pain_point source) has spiked their anxiety and search activity, making them unusually receptive to a trustworthy alternative to their current signal sources.
ideal_customer_profile.note: Mirrors the audience actively targeted by the competitor ads in ads.json (paid-signal fatigue, chart-literacy education, free-course lead-gen).

key_pain_point.problem: Information overload plus directly contradicting expert opinions cause decision paralysis and cognitive overload in solo retail traders — the more they consume, the less decisive they become.
key_pain_point.why_this_is_strongest: It is the pain every competitor in ads.json gestures at but none solves head-on: Quant AI sells a single black-box AI analysis (no track record), Options 101 sells education (a class, not a decision), and the Vietnamese course page sells more information and weekly stock picks (more data). CrowdWisdom is the only offering whose core mechanism — accuracy-weighted consensus from thousands of verified professionals with a public, auditable outcomes page — is a direct remedy. It recasts overload into one decision.

source_and_reasoning.detail: AAII Investor Sentiment Survey: Bearish sentiment hit a 1-Year Bearish High of 66.7% in the week ending 9/10/2026, with Neutral at a record-low ~22-23% — retail investors are abruptly, and contradictorily, polarized.

Finance Magnates ('How AI Overload Affects Retail Traders' Behaviour, Decisions, and Churn') and Global Banking & Finance Review ('The Silent Crisis in Modern Trading: Why More Information Is Not Making Traders Smarter', 2026): overwhelming stimulation impairs decision-making; cognitive overload drives emotional fatigue, overtrading, and impulsive decisions. This is the 'silent crisis' the spot dramatizes.

CrowdWisdom founder (Gilad Bar-Ilan, Medium, 2026): active traders say 'I'm paying for TipRanks, Seeking Alpha, and Investing.com and I still don't know what the difference is between them.' Tools deliver information, not decisions. Quote: 'You don't need more data. You need the collective signal of the world's best traders, distilled and delivered as a ready-to-execute decision.'

source_and_reasoning.type: Competitive gap from ads.json (Meta Ad Library, last 30 days)
source_and_reasoning.detail: Quant AI ad copy: 'You need clarity, not guesswork' — admits the pain, but sells screenshot-to-AI analysis with no public track record. The high-engagement Options 101 (5.5k page likes) sells chart-reading education. CrowdWisdom's transparent, accuracy-weighted consensus + audited outcomes on a public predictions page is the unclaimed high ground.

visual_hook.description: A blender-speed montage of faceless pundits in broadcast boxes, each shouting a different verdict in under 4 seconds: a green 'BUY' card, a red 'SELL' card, a headline 'CRASH IMMINENT', then 'TO THE MOON'. Rapid smash-cuts, raised-desk feel, handheld shake, then ONE beat of dead silence as the last card snaps to 'WHO'S RIGHT?' centered on a dark screen.

scenes.purpose: VISUAL HOOK - expert conflict in 4 seconds
scenes.camera: Handheld shake, 0.6s cuts between broadcast boxes; whip-pan into a hard cut to black
scenes.visual: Rapid-fire montage: three/four talking-head pundit boxes, each throwing a contradictory prediction card at camera (BUY / SELL / CRASH IMMINENT / TO THE MOON). Noise alerts chirp. Last beat: pure black, title card slams in.
scenes.on_screen_text: BUY ▲ / SELL ▼ / CRASH IMMINENT! / TO THE MOON 🚀 — then centered: WHO'S RIGHT?
scenes.sound_design: Stabbing synth stabs + alert pings, then abrupt digital dropout to dead silence

scenes.purpose: PROBLEM - the silent crisis: overload, not opportunity
scenes.camera: Slow push-in on subject, shallow depth of field, cold blue-grey grade
scenes.visual: Low-lit 1am scene. A solo trader (the ICP) hunched at a desk; three monitors full of charts, a news ticker, a Discord/Telegram feed lighting up. Their face is lit by the blue glow, eyes darting, mug of cold coffee, tension headache. Cutaway on their phone: 14 stacked unread alerts.
scenes.voiceover: They told you the problem was finding information. It isn't. You drown in it. Every expert disagrees today, and every one of them sounds sure.
scenes.sound_design: Low drone + phone ping spiral, a heartbeat building

scenes.purpose: THE TRUTH - the market is a crowd, not an oracle
scenes.camera: Pull back, camera floats up out of the small room to a wide abstract data-shot
scenes.visual: Ascend from the trader's screens into an abstract visual: thousands of tiny trader avatars/light-particles orbiting a glowing price ticker (the 'crowd'). A line fills showing Bearish at 66.7% (record 1-year high, week of 9/10) while a bar of Bullish sits opposite. Two pundit AVATARS pop in and shout, then fade — their noise is already inside the crowd's movement.
scenes.voiceover: The single smartest opinion you'll find is still one opinion. But the market, it moves at the speed of a crowd. 66.7% of retail is suddenly bearish — you can feel that panic in the ticker. The ones winning are reading the whole crowd, not one loud voice.

sound_design_notes: Scene 1: stabs/pings then digital dropout. Scene 2: low drone + heartbeat under cold blue grade. Scenes 3-6: tension release into warm resolve, one continuous musical build to the CTA. VO: calm, credible, deliberate — a plain-spoken peer, NOT a hype-man. Pace keeps every VO line under ~9 words/sec so burned-in subtitles stay readable on mobile.
creative_differentiation_note: Distinct from prior 'You're Not Guessing Alone' spot: that concept led with solo-trader loneliness and paid-signal fatigue; this one leads with expert-conflict and decision paralysis, and is anchored to a live, citable market event (AAII 66.7% bearish 1-yr high, wk of 9/10/2026) so the ad feels topical within the 30-day content window.
production_notes: ON-SCREEN STAT: '66.7% bearish' and '73.8% track record' must be re-verified against the live AAII survey snapshot and the CrowdWisdom predictions page immediately before render; swap in audited figures if shifting.
Risk clause: on-screen disclaimer 'Trading involves substantial risk. Not investment advice.' required by ad-policy; place bottom of final card and product scenes.
Shoot/grade: two lighting states (cold blue 1am / warm morning) to dramatize the arc; avatar/pundit boxes can be CGI or stock to avoid real faces.
Vertical 9:16 primary (Reels/TikTok/Shorts); prep a 16:9 cut for in-feed; keep all text within the mobile safe zone (center 2/3).
